text: A longer external moment arm makes the same load harder to move at a joint because it increases which demand?
explanation: External torque rises when the perpendicular distance from the load to the joint axis increases.

text: Which sequence best represents the path of oxygen from the environment to working muscle?
options: Ventilation, diffusion, circulation and tissue extraction
explanation: Oxygen is ventilated into the lungs, diffuses into blood, is transported by circulation and is extracted by tissues.

text: Why is adequate protein important during rehabilitation?
options: It replaces the need for loading
It supports tissue remodelling when energy and training are also adequate
It supplies the fastest fuel for a maximal sprint
explanation: Protein supplies amino acids for remodelling, but recovery also requires appropriate loading, total energy and other nutrients.

text: An athlete continues a difficult rehabilitation programme because it is personally meaningful. Which motivation is most evident?
explanation: Intrinsic motivation involves engaging in an activity because it is personally valued or enjoyable rather than only to obtain an external reward.

text: Which measure is more directly informative about central fat distribution than body mass index alone?
explanation: Waist circumference provides information about abdominal size and central distribution that body mass index alone cannot provide.

text: Why should a rehabilitation programme eventually include the athlete's sport-specific demands?
options: Sport demands are unrelated to injury recurrence
Specific exposure helps restore tolerance to the demands that matter in competition
Sport practice makes strength testing unnecessary
explanation: The final stages of rehabilitation should progressively expose the athlete to relevant speed, force, decision and environmental demands.

text: A landing strategy that increases the time over which a similar force acts will generally increase which quantity?
explanation: Impulse equals force multiplied by time. Changing the time of force application changes the impulse and momentum relationship.

text: Which statement about the three major energy systems during exercise is most accurate?
options: Only one system operates at a time
The oxidative system is irrelevant during sprint recovery
Glycolysis supplies no energy during repeated efforts
All contribute, but their relative contributions change with intensity and duration
explanation: The energy systems overlap continuously; the dominant contribution depends on the work and recovery demands.

text: A physiotherapist and strength coach disagree about an athlete's readiness. What is the best way to resolve the disagreement?
options: Use shared definitions, review the evidence and agree on measurable criteria
Let the most senior person decide without discussion
Remove the athlete from the conversation
explanation: Interdisciplinary decisions improve when the team shares information, defines criteria and communicates uncertainty transparently.

text: Which feature makes overtraining syndrome more concerning than a short planned period of functional overreaching?
options: A persistent decline with broader symptoms and prolonged recovery
explanation: Overtraining syndrome involves persistent maladaptation and prolonged performance decline, not merely a brief response to a training block.

text: A new jump mat is compared with a laboratory force platform. This comparison mainly examines which property?
explanation: Comparing a new measure with an accepted reference method examines criterion-related validity.

text: Why should the same pre-test instructions be used when monitoring a morning readiness measure?
options: To make the measure valid for every purpose
To reduce variation caused by hydration, posture, timing and recent activity
explanation: Standardising timing and conditions reduces avoidable variation and makes changes easier to interpret.

text: Test-retest reliability asks whether a measure is consistent when the same person is tested under similar conditions on different occasions. What is it not?
options: A direct guarantee of clinical validity
explanation: A reliable measure may still fail to measure the intended construct, so reliability alone does not establish validity.

text: A limb symmetry index is 95%, but both limbs are below the team's performance standard. What is the best conclusion?
options: The athlete may be bilaterally under-capacitated despite symmetry
The test should be discarded automatically
The weaker limb is definitely normal
explanation: Relative symmetry can hide bilateral deficits; absolute performance and movement quality should also be considered.

text: Which movement quantity is most directly measured by a gyroscope in an inertial sensor?
explanation: A gyroscope measures angular velocity; an inertial unit may combine this with acceleration and magnetic-orientation data.

text: Why should a performance analyst avoid treating a GPS high-speed-running value as a direct measure of metabolic stress?
options: External load and internal load are identical
Metabolic stress cannot be monitored in sport
It is an external movement measure and does not capture the full internal response
explanation: GPS-derived distance and speed describe external movement; internal response also depends on intensity, fitness, heat, fatigue and context.

text: A wearable reports an unusual recovery score after the athlete changed devices. What should happen before changing training?
options: Check device validity, collection conditions and the athlete's other information
explanation: A device or protocol change can create an apparent change. Data quality and context should be checked before decisions are made.

text: A model predicts injury extremely well in the data used to train it but poorly in a new team. Which problem is most likely?
explanation: A model can learn noise or team-specific patterns in training data and fail when applied to new data; external validation is important.

text: What does a larger standard deviation generally indicate when the mean and units are the same?
options: A lower sample size in every case
More spread of observations around the mean
explanation: Standard deviation describes the spread of observations around the mean in the same units as the measured variable.

text: Training load and injury reports rise together in a dataset. Why can the analyst not conclude that load alone caused every injury?
options: Load has no relationship to health
Causation is proved by any positive correlation
Correlation does not establish causation and other factors may confound the association
explanation: Observational associations may reflect confounding, reverse causation, measurement issues or multiple interacting causes.

text: A risk ratio of 2.0 for an outcome in an exposed group compared with an unexposed group means what?
options: The exposed group had twice the observed risk
The intervention reduced risk to zero
There were two cases in total
explanation: A risk ratio of 2 indicates the observed risk was twice as high in the exposed group relative to the comparison group.

text: Why should a post-intervention performance score be compared with a baseline collected under similar conditions?
options: It guarantees the intervention caused the change
It provides a reference for judging change while reducing interpretation ambiguity
It removes the need for a comparison group
It makes all measures normally distributed
explanation: A comparable baseline helps quantify change, although causal interpretation still depends on design and other evidence.

text: When strength and endurance sessions are both required, what helps reduce unnecessary interference?
options: Plan sequence, spacing, recovery and priorities around the sport calendar
Use the same intensity for every session
explanation: Concurrent training should be sequenced and dosed according to goals, fatigue, recovery and the sport's demands.

text: Which information is most useful for individualising hydration during a long training session?
options: A universal fixed volume for every athlete
Pre- and post-session body mass, fluid intake, duration and environmental conditions
explanation: Sweat-rate planning uses body-mass change, fluid intake, duration and environmental conditions, with attention to sodium and overdrinking risk.

text: Which order is most defensible when an athlete is repeatedly failing to recover between sessions?
options: Review training dose, sleep, food and fluids before adding optional recovery tools
Start with the most expensive device
Ignore the schedule and add more volume
Use passive treatment instead of investigating the cause
explanation: Foundational training, sleep and nutrition factors should be reviewed before optional modalities are added.

text: Periodisation is best described as what?
options: Planned variation of training emphasis over time
explanation: Periodisation organises training variation and progression over time to manage adaptation, fatigue and performance goals.

text: Which approach is most appropriate when an athlete first arrives at moderate altitude?
options: Start maximal intervals to force adaptation
Allow adjustment, monitor symptoms and avoid an immediate large intensity spike
explanation: Altitude changes physiological stress. Early training should be adjusted while symptoms, sleep, hydration and response are monitored.

text: Westward travel usually requires the body clock to make which adjustment?
options: Permanent reversal of day and night
A phase delay, supported by appropriately timed light and sleep
explanation: Westward travel generally requires delaying the circadian phase; timing depends on the destination and competition schedule.

text: Why should low energy availability be considered even when an athlete is not trying to lose weight?
options: It can occur unintentionally when exercise expenditure and intake do not match
It occurs only in athletes with a diagnosed eating disorder
Body mass always identifies it accurately
explanation: Low energy availability may be unintentional and can affect athletes of any sex, sport or body size.

text: A team wants to collect daily wellness data from minors. Which step is essential?
options: Explain purpose, obtain appropriate consent and protect access to the data
Publish individual scores to motivate compliance
Allow unrestricted access to every staff member
explanation: Data collection should have a clear purpose, appropriate consent or assent, limited access, secure storage and transparent communication.

text: In anti-doping education, strict liability means that the athlete is generally responsible for what?
options: Any supplement chosen by the coach but never the athlete
Only substances personally injected by the athlete
What is found in the athlete's sample, subject to the applicable rules and processes
Nothing unless deliberate cheating is proven
explanation: The athlete has responsibility for prohibited substances found in the sample, although results management and applicable defences follow the governing rules.

text: Which coaching choice best supports long-term development in a growing athlete?
options: Prioritise winning over education and wellbeing
Use adult performance standards without adjustment
Individualise load, teach movement skills and monitor growth, health and enjoyment
explanation: Long-term development integrates physical, technical, psychological, educational and health needs rather than short-term results alone.

text: What is the principal Olympic Movement role of a National Olympic Committee?
options: Represent and develop the Olympic Movement within its country
Write the detailed technical rules for every sport
Run only one edition of the Olympic Games
explanation: A National Olympic Committee represents the Olympic Movement nationally and supports participation and development within the Olympic framework.

text: The first modern Olympic Games were held in which city in 1896?
explanation: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896.

text: What is a central purpose of a Sports Authority of India National Centre of Excellence?
options: Provide high-performance training with sports-science and support services
Set the rules of international football
explanation: National Centres of Excellence provide high-performance preparation with coaching, sports science, medical, nutrition and related support.

text: Which use is consistent with the National Sports Development Fund's athlete-support role?
options: Determining a diagnosis without medical assessment
Supporting approved training, equipment or travel for sporting development
explanation: The fund supports sports development and approved athlete preparation needs such as training, equipment and travel.

text: Which statement best reflects the athlete's responsibility under the anti-doping principle of strict liability?
options: The athlete is responsible for prohibited substances found in the sample
Only the doctor can ever be responsible
A supplement label guarantees a clean result
Intent must always be proven before any rule applies
explanation: Strict liability places responsibility on the athlete for prohibited substances detected in the sample, subject to the governing rules and results process.

text: During sample collection, which behaviour best protects the integrity of the process?
options: Leave before the sample is sealed
Follow the instructions, check the sample code and keep the documentation
Ask another athlete to provide the sample
explanation: The athlete should follow the collection process, verify identifiers and retain the required documentation.

text: Which organisation governs the FIFA World Cup?
explanation: Fédération Internationale de Football Association, commonly called FIFA, governs the FIFA World Cup.

text: What is an appropriate organisational response when a workplace sexual-harassment complaint is received?
options: Destroy records after the first conversation
Share the complaint widely to discourage others
Ask the complainant to investigate the respondent alone
Follow the lawful complaint and inquiry process while protecting confidentiality
explanation: A complaint should be handled through the applicable process with impartiality, confidentiality, records and protection from retaliation.

text: Which rotator-cuff muscle is the main internal rotator of the glenohumeral joint?
explanation: Subscapularis is the rotator-cuff muscle that contributes strongly to internal rotation of the shoulder.

text: The Achilles tendon is formed mainly by the tendons of which muscles?
options: Tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus
explanation: The calcaneal or Achilles tendon is formed principally by gastrocnemius and soleus, with contribution from the plantaris in some descriptions.

text: Weakness of pelvic control during single-leg stance is commonly associated with reduced function of which muscle?
explanation: Gluteus medius contributes to hip abduction and frontal-plane pelvic control during single-leg stance.

text: The brachial plexus supplies the principal motor and sensory innervation of which region?
explanation: The brachial plexus provides the major peripheral nerve supply to the upper limb.

text: Compared with the lateral meniscus, the medial meniscus is generally more firmly attached to which structure?
explanation: The medial meniscus is less mobile and has an attachment relationship with the medial collateral ligament, which can influence injury patterns.

text: A faster fall in heart rate during the first minutes after exercise is generally interpreted as what?
options: A sign of poor autonomic recovery in every context
A marker that may reflect better recovery or fitness when measured consistently
A direct measure of muscle damage
explanation: Heart-rate recovery can reflect autonomic recovery and fitness, but it must be measured consistently and interpreted with context.

text: During dynamic aerobic exercise, systolic blood pressure usually does what?
explanation: Systolic pressure generally rises with dynamic exercise as cardiac output increases, while the response should be interpreted clinically.

text: Oxygen deficit refers to the early period of exercise when oxygen consumption is below the level expected for the eventual steady demand. What supplies more energy during this period?
explanation: At exercise onset, oxygen uptake lags behind demand and anaerobic energy contribution is relatively greater.

text: Sweating cools the body most effectively when sweat can do what?
options: Prevent all blood flow to the skin
explanation: Evaporation removes heat from the skin; high humidity and impermeable clothing reduce the effectiveness of sweating.

text: Anaerobic glycolysis can provide ATP rapidly, but high rates of contribution are associated with which challenge?
options: It can contribute to metabolite accumulation and fatigue
explanation: Rapid glycolytic ATP provision is useful during intense work, but associated metabolite changes may contribute to fatigue and recovery demands.

text: The therapeutic effect of an interferential current is commonly produced by the interaction of which currents?
options: A mechanical vibration and a heat lamp
Two direct currents of zero frequency
Two medium-frequency currents with slightly different frequencies
Only a magnetic field with no electrical current
explanation: Interferential therapy uses the interaction of two medium-frequency currents with a difference or beat frequency.

text: What is a common short-term effect of local cryotherapy?
options: Reduced tissue temperature and altered pain or nerve conduction
explanation: Cold can reduce tissue temperature and alter sensation and nerve conduction; it does not guarantee a specific healing outcome.

text: Short-wave diathermy is intended primarily to deliver which type of therapeutic energy?
explanation: Short-wave diathermy uses electromagnetic radiofrequency energy and requires attention to contraindications and metal or electronic devices.

text: Electromyography is used primarily to examine what?
options: Electrical activity associated with muscle activation
explanation: Electromyography records electrical activity associated with muscle activation and can support neuromuscular assessment.

text: An isometric contraction produces force without which visible change?
options: A change in muscle-tendon length at the joint
explanation: In an isometric contraction, muscle force is produced without appreciable joint movement or change in the external muscle-tendon length.

text: During the lowering phase of a controlled squat, the quadriceps primarily perform which action?
options: Eccentric knee-extensor action while lengthening under load
explanation: The quadriceps control knee flexion while lengthening during the lowering phase, which is an eccentric action.

text: A motor-control exercise is initially performed slowly with feedback. Why?
options: To improve awareness and quality before adding speed or complexity
To avoid using the target muscles
explanation: Slow, well-controlled practice can establish movement quality and awareness before speed, load or decision-making demands are increased.

text: Which progression increases balance demand without immediately increasing external load?
options: Add maximal resistance and remove supervision
Reduce visual input or add a controlled cognitive task
Widen the base and use both hands
explanation: Visual, surface and cognitive changes can alter balance demand; the progression must remain appropriate and safe.

text: Which statement best describes a useful flexibility intervention?
options: Painful stretching is always more effective
Every tight structure should be stretched maximally
Its dose and purpose should match the movement limitation and sport need
Flexibility is unrelated to strength and control
explanation: Flexibility work should be targeted, tolerable and integrated with strength and movement control rather than applied as a universal maximal stretch.

text: During a standing balance test, the centre of pressure describes what?
options: The location of the most painful muscle
The athlete's anatomical centre of mass only
The point location of the resultant ground-force distribution
explanation: Centre of pressure is the point of application of the resultant ground reaction force distribution under the foot or support surface.

text: Angular momentum is influenced by angular velocity and which other property?
explanation: Angular momentum is related to moment of inertia and angular velocity, analogous to linear momentum's relation to mass and velocity.

text: A lever in which the fulcrum lies between the effort and the resistance is which class?
explanation: In a first-class lever, the fulcrum is positioned between the effort and resistance.

text: Cadence during gait refers to what?
options: Peak heart rate during a sprint
The distance between the two shoulders
explanation: Gait cadence is commonly expressed as the number of steps taken per minute.

text: Why may allowing controlled hip and knee flexion during landing reduce the abruptness of force application?
options: It can increase the time and movement through which the body absorbs load
explanation: Controlled flexion can increase the time and distance over which mechanical work is absorbed, although technique must remain sport-appropriate.

text: An athlete's belief that they can complete a rehabilitation task successfully is called what?
explanation: Self-efficacy is the belief in one's capability to organise and perform the actions required for a task.

text: Which combination is most characteristic of sport burnout?
options: Exhaustion, reduced accomplishment and sport devaluation
Only one episode of muscle soreness
High motivation with no emotional change
explanation: Burnout is commonly described through exhaustion, a reduced sense of accomplishment and devaluation of the sport experience.

text: A cue directing an athlete to “push the ground away” is primarily an example of what?
explanation: The cue directs attention to the movement effect on the environment, an external focus.

text: Pain or a click during a meniscal provocation test should be interpreted how?
options: As proof of a meniscal tear in every athlete
As proof that the knee is normal
With history and other findings rather than as a stand-alone diagnosis
explanation: Special tests modify clinical probability but should be interpreted with the history, examination and functional presentation.

text: The Finkelstein test is commonly used when assessing suspected involvement of which region?
explanation: Finkelstein-type testing is used in the clinical assessment of radial-sided wrist pain involving the first dorsal compartment.

text: A neurological screen for low-back pain should include which combination?
options: Relevant sensation, myotomes, reflexes and neural tension when indicated
explanation: Neurological examination is guided by symptoms and may include sensation, strength, reflexes and neurodynamic testing.

text: Pain that is severe, constant, non-mechanical and associated with systemic symptoms should prompt what?
options: A conclusion that the athlete is exaggerating
A broader assessment and consideration of medical referral
explanation: Non-mechanical pain with systemic features can indicate serious pathology and requires broader assessment rather than routine progression.

text: After collecting the history and examination findings, what is the next reasoning step?
options: Clear the athlete before discussing goals
Skip directly to a fixed treatment package
Ignore findings that do not fit the first idea
Form and test a working hypothesis while considering safety and referral
explanation: Clinical reasoning involves synthesising findings, testing hypotheses, identifying risk and adapting the plan as new information appears.

text: Which symptom after a head impact should be treated as a red flag requiring urgent escalation?
explanation: Deterioration and repeated vomiting are concerning after head injury and require urgent assessment rather than routine sideline observation.

text: The Doha agreement includes which clinically defined groin pain category?
explanation: The Doha agreement describes adductor-, iliopsoas-, inguinal- and pubic-related groin pain categories based on clinical examination.

text: Which factor should be included in a return-to-sport decision after injury?
options: Only the number of days since injury
Objective capacity, symptoms, sport demands and athlete context
explanation: Return decisions should integrate objective findings, symptoms, sport demands, psychological readiness, context and shared clinical judgement.

text: What distinguishes suspected exertional heat stroke from ordinary exercise fatigue?
options: A desire to stop the session
Central nervous system dysfunction with severe heat illness
explanation: Central nervous system dysfunction in a severely overheated athlete is a key emergency feature requiring rapid cooling and medical care.

text: Which travel plan best protects an athlete competing soon after a time-zone change?
options: Coordinate sleep, light, meals, hydration, movement and training with the itinerary
Use the same sleep schedule regardless of destination
explanation: Travel readiness requires a coordinated sleep, light, nutrition, hydration, movement and training plan matched to the destination.

text: Why is carbohydrate availability especially important before repeated high-intensity training?
options: It prevents the use of all other fuels
It supports glycogen-dependent work and helps maintain training quality
It replaces the need for hydration
explanation: Carbohydrate supports muscle glycogen and high-intensity exercise; the amount should match the training and competition demands.

text: What is the purpose of blinding participants or outcome assessors when feasible in a trial?
explanation: Blinding can reduce expectation and measurement bias, although the practical feasibility depends on the intervention.

text: Why is third-party testing helpful but not an absolute guarantee for an athlete using a supplement?
options: It transfers responsibility away from the athlete
Testing makes a product automatically therapeutic
Testing may reduce contamination risk, but no process removes every risk or replaces informed choice
explanation: Third-party testing can reduce but not eliminate contamination or labelling risk; athletes remain responsible for informed anti-doping decisions.

text: Which finding most supports a proximal hamstring injury in this athlete?
options: Posterior thigh pain with resisted knee flexion and stretch loading
Numbness confined to the little finger
explanation: Posterior thigh symptoms reproduced with hamstring contraction and lengthening support a hamstring-related presentation, while the full differential remains important.
passage: A sprinter feels sudden high posterior-thigh pain during maximal acceleration. Walking is possible, but fast running and long-stride stretching reproduce symptoms. There is no loss of consciousness or neurovascular deficit.

text: Which early rehabilitation choice is most appropriate?
options: Perform repeated maximal sprints to test healing
Protect from provocative high-speed lengthening while maintaining tolerable capacity
Use complete immobilisation regardless of symptoms
explanation: Early management modifies provocative load while preserving safe movement and capacity; later stages progressively restore running exposure.
passage: A sprinter feels sudden high posterior-thigh pain during maximal acceleration. Walking is possible, but fast running and long-stride stretching reproduce symptoms. There is no loss of consciousness or neurovascular deficit.

text: Why should high-speed running be a planned part of later rehabilitation?
options: It replaces strength and trunk control work
It guarantees that recurrence is impossible
It restores exposure to a key sport demand in graded steps
It should be introduced before pain and function are assessed
explanation: Progressive high-speed exposure helps restore the specific demand that caused symptoms, but it must be integrated with strength, control and monitoring.
passage: A sprinter feels sudden high posterior-thigh pain during maximal acceleration. Walking is possible, but fast running and long-stride stretching reproduce symptoms. There is no loss of consciousness or neurovascular deficit.

text: Which combination is most useful before unrestricted sprinting?
options: The athlete's confidence without physical testing
A normal seated knee range only
Symptom response, strength, high-speed exposure and sport-specific function
explanation: Return should combine symptoms, capacity, exposure tolerance, movement quality and the demands of the sport.
passage: A sprinter feels sudden high posterior-thigh pain during maximal acceleration. Walking is possible, but fast running and long-stride stretching reproduce symptoms. There is no loss of consciousness or neurovascular deficit.

text: Which finding is most consistent with lateral elbow tendinopathy?
options: Pain with resisted wrist extension and gripping near the lateral epicondyle
Loss of sensation over the lateral foot
explanation: Lateral elbow tendinopathy commonly presents with load-related lateral elbow pain during gripping and resisted wrist extension.
passage: A tennis player has six weeks of lateral elbow pain that worsens with backhand gripping. There is no neck pain, trauma, swelling or resting neurological deficit.

text: Which early loading plan is most defensible?
options: Avoid all use of the arm indefinitely
Progressive wrist-extensor and gripping load within a monitored symptom response
Perform maximal gripping through sharp pain
Treat only with repeated passive ultrasound
explanation: Progressive tendon loading and modification of provoking tasks are more useful than indefinite rest or passive treatment alone.
passage: A tennis player has six weeks of lateral elbow pain that worsens with backhand gripping. There is no neck pain, trauma, swelling or resting neurological deficit.

text: Which additional finding would make cervical or radial-nerve involvement more important in the differential?
options: Tenderness limited to the tendon region
Neck-related symptoms with neurological change into the arm
explanation: Neck symptoms, neurological findings or symptom distribution beyond the local tendon region should broaden the differential diagnosis.
passage: A tennis player has six weeks of lateral elbow pain that worsens with backhand gripping. There is no neck pain, trauma, swelling or resting neurological deficit.

text: Which return-to-play progression best matches the problem?
options: Use pain score alone without tracking exposure
Return immediately to a full tournament because pain is tolerable
Avoid all racquet-specific work until the next season
Increase gripping volume, stroke intensity and match duration in planned steps
explanation: Sport exposure should progress from controlled volume and intensity toward match demands while monitoring symptoms and capacity.
passage: A tennis player has six weeks of lateral elbow pain that worsens with backhand gripping. There is no neck pain, trauma, swelling or resting neurological deficit.

text: Which finding supports an iliopsoas-related groin pain classification under the Doha terminology?
options: Pain in the iliopsoas region reproduced by resisted hip flexion or hip-flexor stretch
An isolated lateral ankle fracture sign
explanation: Iliopsoas-related groin pain is supported by relevant pain location and pain on resisted hip flexion or hip-flexor stretch.
passage: A football midfielder develops anterior groin pain after repeated kicking. Pain is reproduced with resisted hip flexion and a hip-flexor stretch. There is no fever, abdominal symptom or neurological deficit.

text: Which early load modification is most reasonable?
options: Reduce provocative kicking volume while maintaining tolerable conditioning and progressive strength
Avoid all hip motion for several weeks
Use a single imaging result as the complete diagnosis
explanation: Load should be modified around the provoking demand while capacity is maintained and progressively rebuilt.
passage: A football midfielder develops anterior groin pain after repeated kicking. Pain is reproduced with resisted hip flexion and a hip-flexor stretch. There is no fever, abdominal symptom or neurological deficit.

text: Which new feature should broaden the assessment beyond a local iliopsoas problem?
options: Pain only during resisted hip flexion
Fever, abdominal symptoms or pain unrelated to movement
Local tenderness that follows the expected pattern
explanation: Systemic or non-mechanical symptoms require consideration of other medical or regional causes and possible referral.
passage: A football midfielder develops anterior groin pain after repeated kicking. Pain is reproduced with resisted hip flexion and a hip-flexor stretch. There is no fever, abdominal symptom or neurological deficit.

text: Which criterion is most useful before full-intensity kicking returns?
options: Tolerance of progressive hip-flexion strength and kicking exposure without a concerning response
explanation: Return should progress the relevant strength, range, speed and kicking exposure while monitoring symptoms and function.
passage: A football midfielder develops anterior groin pain after repeated kicking. Pain is reproduced with resisted hip flexion and a hip-flexor stretch. There is no fever, abdominal symptom or neurological deficit.

text: What is the priority when this athlete develops central nervous system dysfunction during hot exercise?
options: Immediate whole-body cooling and emergency activation
Wait for a laboratory temperature before cooling
Give salt tablets and resume running
Place the athlete in a warm room for observation
explanation: Suspected exertional heat stroke requires rapid cooling and emergency management; treatment should not wait for laboratory confirmation.
passage: At a summer tournament, a runner becomes confused, stumbles and collapses after a hard effort. Skin is very hot and the athlete cannot follow simple instructions.

text: Which action should not delay cooling?
options: Removing excess clothing and beginning an effective cooling method
Obtaining a perfect history from every teammate
Waiting for the athlete to request treatment
explanation: Cooling should begin promptly while emergency support is activated; a complete history can be gathered as the response proceeds.
passage: At a summer tournament, a runner becomes confused, stumbles and collapses after a hard effort. Skin is very hot and the athlete cannot follow simple instructions.

text: Why should the event emergency action plan be activated early?
options: It guarantees the diagnosis without assessment
It coordinates trained help, equipment, transport and communication
It allows the athlete to leave without documentation
explanation: An emergency action plan coordinates people, equipment, access, communication and transport during a time-critical event.
passage: At a summer tournament, a runner becomes confused, stumbles and collapses after a hard effort. Skin is very hot and the athlete cannot follow simple instructions.

text: After the athlete is transferred for medical care, what should the team do?
options: Assume the emergency plan worked perfectly without checking
Erase the incident to protect the event's image
Return the athlete to training the next day without review
Document the event and review the response for future prevention
explanation: Accurate documentation and a structured review can identify improvements in prevention, recognition, cooling and communication.
passage: At a summer tournament, a runner becomes confused, stumbles and collapses after a hard effort. Skin is very hot and the athlete cannot follow simple instructions.

text: An athlete can jog but cannot tolerate near-maximal speed without next-day pain. What is the best conclusion?
options: High-speed capacity is not yet restored for unrestricted sport
The athlete should stop all conditioning
Time since injury overrides the response
explanation: The athlete has not yet demonstrated tolerance to a key sport demand, so sprint exposure should continue to progress before unrestricted return.
passage: A football winger is returning after a hamstring injury. Strength is improving and straight-line jogging is symptom-free, but near-maximal sprinting produces posterior-thigh pain later that day. The athlete has an important match in five days.

text: Which next step is most appropriate?
options: Use a maximal sprint test every day
Progress speed and sport-specific running in graded doses while monitoring the response
Clear the athlete because jogging is pain-free
Avoid running until the season is over
explanation: Running speed and volume should be increased progressively, with attention to immediate and next-day symptoms and movement quality.
passage: A football winger is returning after a hamstring injury. Strength is improving and straight-line jogging is symptom-free, but near-maximal sprinting produces posterior-thigh pain later that day. The athlete has an important match in five days.

text: Why should the upcoming match deadline not be the only basis for clearance?
options: A calendar date measures strength directly
A deadline does not demonstrate restored capacity or acceptable risk
Athlete goals are irrelevant to decision-making
explanation: The decision should integrate capacity, response, sport demands, alternatives, uncertainty and athlete goals rather than a deadline alone.
passage: A football winger is returning after a hamstring injury. Strength is improving and straight-line jogging is symptom-free, but near-maximal sprinting produces posterior-thigh pain later that day. The athlete has an important match in five days.

text: How should the team communicate the current recommendation?
options: Hide the delayed pain to protect selection
Let the athlete choose without explaining the risk
Explain the findings, uncertainty and staged options, then decide collaboratively
explanation: Transparent communication of findings, uncertainty, options and consequences supports shared decision-making and athlete welfare.
passage: A football winger is returning after a hamstring injury. Strength is improving and straight-line jogging is symptom-free, but near-maximal sprinting produces posterior-thigh pain later that day. The athlete has an important match in five days.
